name: Voltas Ltd
title: Voltas Ltd - 500575 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 volumes strong (RAC +32%) but margins squeezed by RM/FX shock; 14% price hikes taken vs 18% cost inflation, plus 5-7% from Oct, and channel inventory cut to ~3 weeks. Voltbek EBITDA breakeven now targeted by next FY.

summary.headline: Voltas Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose to INR48 crore (vs INR32 crore) on 32% RAC volume growth, but margins remain under pressure from input cost inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income rose to INR2,746 crore from INR2,412 crore, with PBT of INR83 crore (vs INR54 crore) and net profit of INR48 crore (vs INR32 crore). RAC volumes grew 32% and UCP revenue grew 29%, with RAC market share at 17.4% YTD September 2026, up about 1.5 points. Management said margins were hit by a sharp, prolonged rise in commodity, freight and currency costs during the season, with about 18% cost inflation against about 14% price increases taken so far. A further 5-7% price increase was implemented from October 2026 to cover the gap. Management guided that Q3 and Q4 should show year-on-year profit improvement, with Q4 the key quarter.

segments.name: Segment A - Unitary Cooling Products (RAC, CAC, Home Comfort, Commercial Refrigeration)
segments.commentary: UCP revenue grew 29% with RAC volume up 32%; management said segment profitability improved YoY but did not give a segment margin figure. Commercial Refrigeration was flat; Home Comfort grew healthily; Commercial AC grew steadily.

segments.name: Voltbek Home Appliances
segments.commentary: Recorded its highest Q2 sales in value and volume; YTD market share about 8.8% in washing machines, 7% in refrigerators and 14.9% in semi-automatic washing machines (No. 2). Management targets EBITDA break-even by next financial year, and said recent cost shocks had set back recovery.

segments.name: Segment B - Electro-Mechanical Projects and Services (EMPS)
segments.commentary: Net margin for the quarter was about 2.5-3% after one-offs and other debits, against a long-term target of 4-6%. Management is selectively booking orders; the order book exceeds INR6,800 crore. Sidra guarantee cancellation affected this segment.

segments.name: Segment C - Engineering Products and Services
segments.commentary: Reported high double-digit revenue growth, driven by crushing and screening equipment, O&M contracts, stable African operations and textile machinery spinning solutions and aftermarket.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q3 and Q4 FY27 to show YoY profit improvement vs the same quarters last year; Q4 is the largest quarter, with channel stocking expected in January-March on a hotter summer forecast.

Additional 5-7% price increase implemented from October 2026 (Q3) to cover further cost increases; management said this covers the cost increase, with a 3-4% margin gap expected to be corrected from Q3.
UCP aspirational EBIT margin of 8-9% was referenced by an analyst; management did not give a fresh percentage target and said it will not forecast margins for a small quarter.
EMPS long-term EBITDA margin target remains 4-6%; the company guided Q2 net impact at about 2.5-3%.
Voltbek targets EBITDA break-even by next financial year (FY28).

Management plans to run the Sri City/south facility (about 1.5 million units capacity, operational since August 2024) on a 12-month basis, with OEM outsourcing to cover gaps; target mix about 75-80% in-house and about 20% outsourced on an annual basis.
Leadership transition: Jayant Balan to succeed Mukundan Menon as Managing Director from 25 May 2027, after Menon retires on 24 May 2027.
capex_capacity: South (Sri City) facility started operations in August 2024 with capacity of about 1.5 million units; intent is uniform production through the year to avoid under-absorption, with no material under-absorption in H1 FY27.
Management highlighted localisation of compressors as a strategic priority and said it is evaluating manufacturing partnerships; no capex amount was given.
Installed base cited at about 26 million units, with customer database of about 20 million customers.
New Voltbek product lines planned: frost-free refrigerators and fully automatic washing machines.
demand_pricing: RAC: YTD September 2026 market share 17.4%, up about 1.5 points; lead over No. 2 brand at 4.2 points vs 1.2 points a year earlier.
Price actions: about 14% price increase taken this season (including BEE energy-label change from January 2026), against about 18% cost inflation; further 5-7% from October.

Industry dynamics: about 70% of RAC calendar-year sales fall in January-June; organised trade (about 70 regional retailers) and modern trade (about 35% of volume) lock prices for the season from February, while commodity and currency costs moved sharply.

Cost pressures named: compressors, copper, aluminium, PCBs and motors (locked-in purchase prices), plus ocean freight (roughly doubled), USD and RMB exposure, and monthly-priced plastics and insulation.
Channel inventory at end-Q2 about three weeks, vs four to six weeks a year earlier, per management.
Hedging is done on a 3-4 month landed-cost horizon, monitoring forward premiums.
Management highlighted a fragmented market with about 60 brands, of which 15-20 have share above 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Adjusted EBITDA fell about 40% despite strong RAC and CAC volumes; when does operating leverage in UCP appear, and is share being bought at the cost of margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY profitability improved across verticals including Segment A, Q2 is seasonally soft, and operating leverage should come through in Q3 and Q4 EBIT.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the RAC industry fail to pass on cost increases, and how long are prices locked?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukundan Menon said prices are locked from February for 4-6 months with organised trade and modern trade (about 35% of volume); the volatility hit the season, so the industry is constrained. About 14% price increase taken against 18% cost inflation, with a further 5-7% announced.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company focus on market share or on margin percentage going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises market share and absolute gross margin quantum over gross margin percentage; the lead over No. 2 is 4.2 points YTD.

qa_highlights.question: When will Voltbek reach EBITDA break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets EBITDA break-even by next financial year, though recent commodity shocks have set back recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 14% price hike include the 5-7% announced hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed that the 14% includes the BEE change and the 5-7% is additional, implemented from October (Q3); total hikes are around 18%, matching cost inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Is there under-absorption at the Sri City facility?
qa_highlights.answer: No material under-absorption in H1 FY27; the company intends to run the factory for 12 months and outsource to OEMs where gaps arise.

qa_highlights.question: How much channel inventory is there?
qa_highlights.answer: About three weeks at end-Q2 versus four to six weeks a year earlier.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Q3 price increases sticking and on commodity, currency and freight costs; management said a West Asia de-escalation would speed margin recovery.
EMPS margins were about 2.5-3% in Q2, well below the 4-6% long-term band; execution and the Sidra-related exposure need monitoring.
Voltbek remains loss-making; break-even target is FY28.
Currency exposure: forward premiums rose, and hedging is limited to a 3-4 month horizon.
Q4 channel stocking, El Nino-driven summer and the BEE replacement cycle are key to the year's profitability.
Management did not provide a quantified UCP margin target for FY27; watch for next quarter's guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on market share and long-term positioning but cautious on near-term margins, which management attributed to an unusually volatile cost environment and season-locked pricing. Management was evasive on specific margin percentages and quantified timelines, repeatedly pointing to YoY improvement and Q4 instead.
key_quotes: So, we remain committed to the fact that market share growth has to happen for sure.
This kind of volatility we have never seen in the last many years where during the season, starting from February, going right up to July, August, things have gone so completely haywire.
Our idea is to get an EBITDA break-even sometime by next financial year, and I think directionally we are going towards that.
The channel inventory is much lower than what it was last year.

growth.why: Management guides Q3 and Q4 FY27 profit above last year's levels, backed by a further 5-7% price increase from October and expected channel stocking in Jan-Mar, though no quantified revenue growth guidance was given and margins remain under cost pressure (about 18% cost inflation vs about 14% price taken).

mgmt.note: Jayant Balan to succeed Mukundan Menon as MD from 25 May 2027 after Menon retires on 24 May 2027; no growth plan stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided YoY profit improvement in Q3 and Q4 with a further 5-7% price rise from October against a 3-4% margin gap; PAT already rose to INR48 crore from INR32 crore, though cost inflation of about 18% vs about 14% price taken keeps margins under pressure.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sri City facility (about 1.5 million units) already running since August 2024 with no material under-absorption in H1 FY27; no new plant or line was announced, only Voltbek product lines with no timing.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: RAC volumes grew 32% YoY in Q2 with RAC share at 17.4% YTD (up about 1.5 points) and a 4.2-point lead over No. 2; Q4 channel stocking expected Jan-Mar on a hotter summer forecast.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management flagged localisation of compressors as a strategic priority and is evaluating manufacturing partnerships, but gave no capex amount; the south facility is running with outsourcing to cover gaps, so utilisation pressure is not clearly acute.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantified revenue or margin guidance and was evasive on margin percentages, so an upgrade has no basis in the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cost inflation of about 18% against about 14% price taken, ocean freight roughly doubled, and forward premiums rising; Q4 profit improvement depends on the 5-7% price rise sticking and on Q4 channel stocking.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Voltbek plans frost-free refrigerators and fully automatic washing machines, but no launch date or capacity was given.

rows.label: Voltbek EBITDA break-even
rows.why: Management targets EBITDA break-even by next financial year, but recent cost shocks have set back recovery and the unit remains loss-making.

rows.label: Further 5-7% RAC price increase from October
rows.why: Already implemented from October 2026 to close a 3-4% margin gap against about 18% cost inflation vs about 14% taken so far.

rows.label: EMPS margin recovery toward 4-6%
rows.why: Q2 net margin was about 2.5-3% vs a 4-6% long-term target; order book over INR6,800 crore but management is selectively booking orders.

tone.note: Management was confident on RAC market share and long-term positioning but cautious and evasive on near-term margin percentages, pointing to YoY improvement and Q4; analysts pressed on the adjusted EBITDA fall of about 40%, margin versus share trade-off, and Voltbek break-even timing.
